summary.text: Lee McInnis is a retired U.S. Army veteran and Defense Intelligence Community officer and the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 3rd Congressional District. An Alabama native and Auburn University graduate, he served in the Army as an Arabic linguist, worked 28 years in defense intelligence, and later taught at the college level. He has not previously held elected office; his campaign emphasizes health care access in rural Alabama, education, affordability, fair taxes and veterans' care.

paragraphs.text: Born in Birmingham and raised in Homewood, Alabama; graduated from Homewood High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1983) from Auburn University, then, after Army service using the GI Bill, a master's degree (1987) studying communications and international relations.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1983 to 1989, trained as an Arabic linguist.

Spent a 28-year career in the Defense Intelligence Community, with extended time overseas in Qatar, Bahrain, Iraq, and Afghanistan; he reports receiving the Joint Staff Civilian Commendation Medal and the Defense Intelligence Agency's Director Intelligence Medal. Describes his work as including serving as an intelligence officer and lead instructor.
Describes retiring when his wife's job moved the family to Augusta, Georgia, and taking a job teaching at a local college; the couple later settled in Lee County, where he lives in Opelika.
Returned to Auburn University and earned a master's degree in history in 2024.
Announced his candidacy at the Opelika Public Library in late 2025; he has no prior campaigns or offices listed. Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary.
Is affiliated with Indivisible Auburn/Opelika, the NAACP (Branch 5038), Auburn United Methodist Church, the National Eagle Scout Association, and the American Legion.
